html:
The Isaaq genocide was the killing of members of the Isaaq clan in northern Somalia by the army of Siad Barre between 1987 and 1989, at its worst when Hargeisa was bombed in 1988.

The Somali National Movement, an Isaaq rebel group, attacked northern cities in May 1988. The government replied by bombing and shelling Hargeisa and Burao, flattening much of them, and killing civilians as they fled. Estimates of the dead range from tens of thousands to around 200,000, and hundreds of thousands fled to Ethiopia.

The killings turned the north against the union of 1960. When Siad Barre fell, the north declared itself Somaliland. Mass graves are still being found.
sum: The Isaaq genocide was the killing of members of the Isaaq clan in northern Somalia by the army of Siad Barre between 1987 and 1989, at its worst when Hargeisa was bombed in 1988.
